review_state_policy: Normal review decisions are approval or rejection, not pending. Unconfirmed associations are excluded until source clarification; this is not a definitive mismatch finding. Original scores and documentary hold reasons are retained.

changes.reason: The registry design declares SCREENING. Its only primary outcome is the number allocated to each study over 4 weeks. The summary explicitly sends screened participants onward to GZP1/NCT06972459 or GZP2/NCT06972472. This allocation record is not a further independent treatment trial; GZP2 is already attached.

The registry design declares SCREENING and the sole primary outcome is allocation to ISAs. Its own summary calls this the CWMM screening record. Treatment of interest belongs to LAA2/NCT06603571, which the sponsor identifies as the actual eloralintide/tirzepatide study. Do not count this screening record as an additional tirzepatide treatment trial.

Exclude until source clarification establishes the named intervention scope; not a definitive mismatch finding. There is a named 73-person tirzepatide exposure cohort and body-weight/BMI secondary outcomes, but the detailed description explicitly pools semaglutide and tirzepatide as a class and says the aim is class-level early hepatic/metabolic index response rather than comparing individual agents. The registry does not establish a separately tested tirzepatide weight effect. Preserve uncertainty instead of treating pooled class exposure as verified single-treatment evidence.

The registry itself distinguishes VLCD 600–800 kcal/day from LCD 800–1000 kcal/day and states its objective is LCD. Experimental arm and intervention description explicitly prescribe 800–1000 kcal/day for 8 weeks. A broad calorie-restriction synonym would change the named intervention.

Exclude until source clarification establishes the named intervention scope; not a definitive mismatch finding. The registry names low-energy diet plus physical activity. The original protocol prescribes approximately 800 kcal/day, but itself distinguishes prior VLED work under 800; the primary results report specifies 800–820 kcal/day. This is a real diabetes-remission intervention, but its equivalence to the current specifically named VLCD claim should not be assumed from total-diet-replacement synonyms. Resolve the claim scope, not the outcome.

Exclude until source clarification establishes the named intervention scope; not a definitive mismatch finding. The primary report explicitly identifies NCT04805996 and specifies Modifast 820–890 kcal/day for 12 weeks, describing a low-calorie TDR intervention. Weight and HbA1c are co-primary, so indication is clear; the specifically named very-low-calorie category is not. Do not silently broaden the card to all TDR.

Exclude until source clarification establishes the named intervention scope; not a definitive mismatch finding. Registry intervention and primary report specify low-energy TDR at approximately 860 kcal/day. Its safety aim in a diabetes-remission program is legitimate and not a reason to exclude. The unresolved point is whether this calorie category belongs to the current specifically named VLCD card; do not infer it from similar weight-management intent.

Exclude until source clarification establishes the named intervention scope; not a definitive mismatch finding. The registry describes a hypocaloric TDR regimen of approximately 800–850 kcal/day with food reintroduction. Diabetes remission is primary. The record does not call its tested regimen VLCD; current card scope needs resolution before treating this dose/category as synonymous. Do not reject merely for including routine lifestyle support.
